A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SceneSplit research, with matching core methodology and retained experiments. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack evaluations on three commercial T2V models, component ablations, semantic analyses, and an appendix evaluation on LTX-Video.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds evaluations on Kling v1.0 and Sora2, RPG-RT comparisons, and robustness and efficiency experiments.

M1.justification: The Scene Splitting, Scene Manipulation, and Strategy Update procedure, Algorithm 1, and appendix prompt/code implementations remain unchanged. Alternative component models and stronger paraphrasing are experimental variants; the proposed default procedure is retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same stated T2VSafetyBench coverage: 220 prompts across the same 11 safety categories. The added target models and ablations extend model settings and analyses without introducing a new dataset, domain, or generation task.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds RPG-RT as a competing attack on all five commercial targets, including the three evaluated in v1. Previously, the main comparison included only the T2VSafetyBench prompt baseline. This substantially strengthens the scope of direct method comparison; the LTX-Video comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds Kling/Sora2 settings and an RPG-RT protocol specifying Veo2 fine-tuning, detector/evaluator handling, and a 15-modification limit. New experiments vary initialization, component models, retrieval thresholds, and paraphrasing intensity, and introduce attempt-count and runtime metrics. The original sampling, default iteration budgets, and success threshold remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds efficiency analyses in Tables 7 and 10; initialization, component-model, and threshold robustness in Appendix C; successful-attack scene-count distributions and a paraphrasing–fidelity comparison in Appendix D; and additional qualitative cases in Appendix I. The original ablations and semantic/output-space analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The semantic-similarity variance reporting in v1 Table 10 is retained in v2 Table 12. No new repeated-run counts, seeds, ASR uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported. The fixed/non-fixed initialization comparison changes experimental conditions rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original Table 1 scores and matched ablation and LTX-Video results remain unchanged. New results include SceneSplit ASRs of 78.6% on Kling and 68.6% on Sora2, plus RPG-RT comparisons. Added analyses report 77.3% ASR with non-fixed initialization and 80.9% ASR/0.5051 semantic similarity under over-paraphrasing versus 78.2%/0.5308 under the standard setting, alongside new runtime and attempt-count results.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains the same divergence definition in Equation 1 and its mathematical explanation. No new or revised formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations appear; the additions are empirical analyses and interpretations.

C1.justification: The three contribution bullets and central claims remain unchanged: a black-box narrative attack whose scene combinations constrain generation toward harmful outputs and bypass T2V safety filters. The abstract and conclusion incorporate additional target-specific results and baseline support for these retained claims.

C2.justification: Sections 3.1–3.2 newly distinguish attacks on text preprocessing filters from video postprocessing defenses. Added discussions explain initialization and component-model robustness, retrieval sensitivity, claimed four-to-five-scene optimality, runtime overhead, and the attack-success/semantic-fidelity tradeoff. The original identity-preservation limitation is retained, moving from Appendix E to G.

D1.justification: v2 documents RPG-RT's Veo2 fine-tuning, detector/evaluator handling, and modification budget, and supplies runtime information in Tables 7 and 10. Existing SceneSplit defaults and appendix implementation listings remain unchanged; no new code or data access resource is specified.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for RPG-RT, its detector discussion, Kling, and Sora2. Section 2.1 explicitly acknowledges conceptual similarity to T2VSafetyBench's temporal risks. The broader related-work discussion and attribution of the strategy-library concept to AutoDAN-Turbo remain intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained. Changes include localized method/result explanations, acknowledgements and an ethics statement, inserted appendix sections, updated cross-references, and author affiliation/contact and publication-header edits. There is no extensive rewriting of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands to five targets and three methods per target, using numbered categories and substantially smaller text. Figure 3 adds Kling/Sora2 examples; Figure 2 corrects its strategy illustration and expands its caption. New analysis tables and Figures 8–9 substantially expand the displays, while older figures and tables are redistributed.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important weakness in v1's competitive validation by adding RPG-RT with a reported matched modification budget. Broader target-model tests and controlled robustness, efficiency, and semantic-fidelity analyses substantially strengthen the evidence and expose practical tradeoffs. ASR uncertainty remains unreported, successful-attack counts alone do not establish optimal scene depth, and Table 1 becomes harder to read, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial validation gains.
